problems: e88: axle ↔ bar is not a compatible pair
notes: The page's schema only holds pieces/other_joins, so the fields are mapped onto the graph: pieces are in parts and each rests_on is a joined edge.
Page 2 also shows the pilot minifig (helmet, goggles, torso, legs). It has no entries in the parts list, so no pieces were recorded for it.
Step 1: the red 2x10 plate (b1) has a yellow inverted wedged brick (b2) pushed onto its end. I identified b2 as lego-4856a from the picture, and it could instead be lego-4855. b2 rests on b1.

Step 2: the two yellow wedged slope bricks (b3 right, b4 left) go on either side of the plate, with the red studs still showing between them. I identified them as lego-43720 and lego-43721. The illustration is ambiguous, so they might also touch b2. I listed them as resting on b1 only.

Sub-assembly boxed on page 3: a black 2x4 plate (b5) gets four reddish-brown round plates in the outer corner positions (b6-b9). A second round plate goes on each of those (b10-b13), giving four stacks of two.

Step 3: the sub-assembly goes under the red 2x10 plate (b1). I assumed b1's bottom clutches the four free middle studs of b5, with the stacks standing either side of the plate. The edge b1-b5 records this.
Step 4: the yellow rear hull piece (b14) is a guess at lego-4855. I could not tell which earlier pieces it touches and listed only b1.

Step 5: the grey 2x2 plate (b15) is placed in the cockpit recess and listed on b1 only. The black plate (b16) at the rear sits on b14. I guessed it is a 1x2 plate (lego-3023), and the type is uncertain.
The mapping to pieces/other_joins is the same as on page 2: rests_on becomes a joined edge.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge, and other_joins are joined edges with ports.

Step 6: I read the black plates as four 2x4 plates (lego-3020). Two cover the rear, and one sits on each side of the cockpit. The side pair is assumed to sit on the yellow wedged bricks b3 and b4, and which one goes on which is a guess. The rear pair is assumed to sit on b14 and b1. The plate types could also be 1x4 plates (lego-3710).
Step 7: the grey seat (b21) sits at the back of the cockpit over the red plate b1.

Step 8, boxed steps 1-2: a clipped bar (lego-48729a) is clipped onto the handle of the dark grey brick (lego-30236) as a joystick. The brick then goes on the cockpit floor beside the seat. I listed it on b1 only, and the actual support is uncertain.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge, and other_joins are joined edges with ports.

Boxed steps 1-3 build the propeller shaft. The axle (b25) goes through the pin hole of one Technic brick (b24). The bush (b26) goes on the axle. A second Technic brick (b27) goes on the axle end beside the first, so the two sit side by side as a 2x2 block.

Step 9: the shaft block goes on the rear black plates, with the axle pointing out the back. I assumed it rests on both b17 and b18, though the picture may show only part of it on each. Axle stays free to turn in the bricks (revolute); bush is fixed on it.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
Step 10 adds the lower wings. They are single reddish-brown 12x3 wedge plates, one on each side, lying on top of the round-plate stacks from page 3.
I took the near wing (viewed with the nose to the right) as the plane's right wing, lego-47398. The far one is the left wing, lego-47397.
Which pair of stacks is on which side is not shown. I assumed b10/b11 are on the far side and b12/b13 on the near side. The wing's actual contact with stacks may differ.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
Step 11 widens each lower wing with a second reddish-brown 12x3 wedge plate of the opposite handedness, so the wing ends up wide with a squared tip.
The far wing (b28, left) gets a right wedge (b30). The near wing (b29, right) gets a left wedge (b31).
I assumed each new plate overlaps and clutches only the wing plate it is added to, not the fuselage. The offset and overlap between the two plates is hard to read in the picture.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.

Step 12 builds up the fuselage sides, with the same parts on each side: a yellow 1x4 brick at the rear, a yellow 1x6 plate along the cockpit, and a grey clip plate (lego-6019) at the front end beside the cockpit.
I assumed b17 and b20 are on the near side and b18 and b19 on the far side. In fact the manual does not show this clearly.
Support relationships are guessed. The 1x6 plates are listed on a rear plate and a side plate, and each clip plate on its side plate. The side plates may also cover the wedged bricks b3/b4 below.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
Step 13 adds the same two parts to each lower wing: a black 1x4 plate across the wing, bridging both wedge plates, and a yellow round 2x2 tile at the wing tip.
The near wing gets b38 and b40. The far wing gets b39 and b41.
Each bridges both wedge plates of its wing, as the picture suggests.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
Step 14 adds yellow 1x2x1 panels as cockpit walls, on the yellow 1x6 plates beside the seat.
Only some panels are fully visible. I assumed two per side, which uses all four lego-4865a in the parts list. The near-side pair is on b34 and the far-side pair on b35.
Their exact positions along the plates are a guess.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
The 2x box on page 11 builds a clip plate (lego-6019) with a black 1x1 plate (lego-3024) on top, twice.

Step 15 shows one copy being lowered onto the dark grey handle brick (b22) behind the seat. I assumed the second copy goes on b22's other stud. The arrows could also mean the second goes by the existing side clip. This is uncertain.
The clip plates here are not yet attached to any bar in the drawing.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
Step 16 covers the nose with black plates. I read this as two 1x4 plates (lego-3710), and the real arrangement may differ.
A third black 1x4 plate runs along the far side of the cockpit. The arrangement is uncertain, and I used lego-3710 because these are the black plates left in the parts list.
Their supports (b2, b19, b20, b35) are guessed from the picture.
The reddish-brown cheese slope (lego-54200) is lowered onto the black 1x1 plate (b47) from page 11.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.

Boxed steps 1-3 build the tail assembly. A reddish-brown 4x4 cut-corner wedge plate (b55) goes onto a reddish-brown 2x2 towball plate (b54). A yellow 2x2 sloped brick (b56) goes on top, and a black 1x4 grooved tile (b57) tops it. The tile is a guess (lego-2431), and the picture could also show the reddish-brown grille tile lego-2412b.

Step 17: the tail goes onto the black nose plates (b50, b51), at the right-hand end of the drawing. That is the rear of the plane, since the propeller shaft is at the left end. I assumed b54 sits on b50 and b51.
The towball is not yet used by any joined part.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge; this page has no stacked pieces, only clip joins.
Step 18's box shows the pickaxe (lego-3841) being clipped onto the far-side clip plates, so that is its main step.
The finished picture also shows a shovel (lego-3837) clipped on the near side. The box does not show it, but the shovel is not on earlier pages, so I added it here.
Each tool is gripped by two clips along its handle. Near side: b36 and b46. Far side: b37 and b48.
Which clips hold which tool is a guess from the drawing's perspective.
Page 15 (step 19) adds the backpack, sextant and binoculars as minifig accessories. The arrow points them at the second minifigure seated in the rear cockpit.
That minifigure and its torso, legs and head are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded as nodes. The accessories therefore have no joins to other recorded pieces.
The backpack goes on the figure's back, and the sextant and binoculars are held in its hands.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge.
Step 20 adds two yellow 2x4 sloped bricks (lego-3037), the only two in the parts list: a cowl over the shaft block at the front and a deck over the black plates at the rear.
The front slope is assumed to span b32, b33 and the shaft bricks b24 and b27. The rear slope is assumed to sit on the black plates b50, b51 and b52, next to the tail assembly.
This page has no box or part callout. The identification of the pieces and their supports is inferred from the finished picture and is uncertain.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge, and other_joins are joined edges with ports.
Step 21 builds the engine: a yellow Technic cylinder (lego-41531) with two exhaust pipes (lego-40620). Each pipe's pin goes into one of the cylinder's pin holes, on the near and far sides.
The cylinder then slides onto the front of the propeller axle (b25). The catalogue entry for lego-41531 has only a bar port, so I joined the axle to bar.1 and assumed it grips the axle.
The cylinder sits against the yellow cowl slope (b63), recorded as a contact.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge, and other_joins are joined edges with ports.

Step 22 adds a pair of reddish-brown tail wings (lego-2340) on the black plates across the lower wings (b38, b39). It also adds the reddish-brown tail fin (lego-3587) on the tail slope (b56). The 2340 and 3587 assignment is inferred from the shapes and the parts list.

Two clear 1x2 bricks (lego-3065) are placed side by side as a windscreen on the shaft bricks, assumed to be b24 and b27. This conflicts with my earlier guess that the cowl b63 covers those bricks, which was uncertain.
The grey bush (lego-32123b) is pushed onto the front of the propeller axle b25, ready for the propeller.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge, and other_joins are joined edges with ports.
The boxed sub-assembly is a red round dome brick (lego-30367b) pressed onto a yellow round plate (lego-4032a), forming the spinner.
The black 3-blade propeller (lego-30332) is pushed onto the axle b25 against the grey bush b73, and then the spinner is pushed onto the axle end.
I joined only the yellow plate to the axle. The red dome's axle holder may also grip it, but that is not shown.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge. Page 20 is a separate sub-assembly, the upper wing. It is not attached to the fuselage yet.
Steps 1-2: two reddish-brown 12x3 wedge plates (b78 left, b79 right) are laid on a yellow 2x6 plate (b77), tapering outward in a V.
Step 3: two more wedges of opposite handedness (b80 right on b78, b81 left on b79) widen each half, as on the lower wing.

Step 4: a round yellow 2x2 tile (b82, b83) goes on each wing tip, and a yellow 3x4 wedge plate (b84) goes at the centre. The 3x4 wedge's support is assumed to be the top wedges b80 and b81. The handedness assignment is a guess.
Step 24 adds no new pieces. It attaches the finished upper wing from page 20 onto the plane, above the lower wings.
I assumed the yellow 2x6 plate (b77) is on the underside of the upper wing. It then clutches the tops of the two reddish-brown wing struts (b70 near, b71 far) that stand on the lower wings.
This is inferred from the finished picture, where the yellow wedge plate (b84) appears on top of the upper wing.
Same mapping as before: rests_on is a joined edge, and other_joins are joined edges with ports.
Step 25 builds the landing gear in the box: a reddish-brown 2x4 plate with pins (lego-30157) with a wheel (lego-30155) pressed onto each pin and a tyre (lego-3483) fitted on each wheel.

The plane is shown upside down. The gear plate goes on the underside of the fuselage, so I assumed its studs clutch the bottom of the black 2x4 plate b5 (the plate with the round-plate stacks), which is recorded as a joined edge.
I could not see exactly which pieces the gear plate touches, so this attachment is a guess.
Step 26 shows the finished biplane with the stickers applied: a roundel on each of the four wing-tip round tiles (b40, b41, b82, b83) and the "4778" stripes on the tail fin (b72).
The sticker sheet (lego-53466) is a single part. I recorded it as one node joined to the stickered parts, as a stick join. It is not a stack, and the stickers should go on the bottom of each tile.
The plane is turned right side up again, with the pilot minifigure seated in the cockpit. The minifigure is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded as a node.
Page 24 is the last page.
Page 24 is advertising for the LEGO Universe website, shop and club. It has no building step, so it adds nothing.

The 14 pieces b91-b105 close the parts-list shortfall. The tail, hull, cockpit rim and engine in the drawings are crowded and partly hidden, and I did not recognise these pieces at the time. Their positions are my best guesses and weakly supported, so I attached each to a plausible supporting piece.

The second cheese slope (b101) goes on the second black 1x1 plate (b49), mirroring b53 on b47. The second 4x4 cut-corner wedge (b99) is the other tailplane, next to b55. The hinge slope (b102) and hinge tile (b103) are a hinged tail piece. The other yellow pieces (4854, 3660, 3623, 6231, 3039) fill hull, rim and cowl gaps.

lego-3020 is one over the parts list: I used five (b5, b17-b20) but the list has four. Pieces cannot be removed in this reply, so b5, b17-b20 stay as given. One of them, most likely b20 (a side plate), is really another black plate type or the 3023 I placed on b100, and the extra 3020 should be treated as a misidentification.

The accessories b60-b62 were isolated pieces because the seated pilot minifigure is not in the parts list. They are now joined to the model by contact edges to the seat (b21), where the pilot sits. This fixes the disconnected groups.
The pilot minifigure still has no node, since its parts are not in the inventory.
